tier_reason: First-party README timing table against icu::UnicodeString::caseCompare; the benchmark code is public (test/bench.cpp, CMake target utf8_bench) but no CPU, compiler, flags, ICU version or run count is given, and no committed version of bench.cpp prints the README's section headers, so the published output came from an uncommitted variant. Claim downgraded because the benchmark design inflates the ratios (pointer-equality short-circuit, ICU charged for char*-to-UTF-16 construction, simple vs full case folding).

corrections.claimed_speedup: README headline: '5x-10x faster than icu::UnicodeString::caseCompare'. README timing table (single run, total ms): generated UTF-8 strings 225 ms vs 3604 ms for icu::UnicodeString::caseCompare (strcasecmp 368 ms); generated ASCII strings 194 ms vs 4486 ms (strcasecmp 360 ms); generated worst-case matching UTF-8 strings 3069 ms vs 12730 ms (strcasecmp 1988 ms). Ratios about 16.0x, 23.1x and 4.1x faster than ICU, and 1.54x slower than strcasecmp in the worst case (derived from page data). These ratios overstate the per-comparison gain: in test/bench.cpp every loop iteration times a call comparing a string with itself (same pointer), which ucstrncasecmp returns from after strlen/strnlen via an 's == t' check while ICU does full work; each ICU call constructs icu::UnicodeString objects from char* (UTF-8 to UTF-16 conversion of both strings) before comparing; and on random strings ucstrcasecmp exits at the first differing byte while ICU must convert whole strings. On the matching workload the per-comparison advantage on real work is therefore likely smaller than 4.1x, possibly near 2x (estimate, not measured).
corrections.workload: test/bench.cpp: a table of 1,000,000 generated strings of STRING_SIZE 30 (bytes for random strings, code points for matching pairs), traversed TABLE_TRAVERSALS 10 times; each iteration times one self-comparison (same pointer) and one comparison against the neighbouring string; wall-clock total via std::chrono::system_clock in ms. Random 'UTF-8' strings are mostly ASCII (2% chance per position of a 2-4 byte sequence); ASCII strings are printable 0x20-0x7E; matching pairs are built from simple case-fold From/To pairs below U+2000 so they match over their full length. The README's three section names do not match any committed bench.cpp revision (initial commit 5746d91 and HEAD print 'Generated Matching UTF-8 strings', 'Generated Tricky matching UTF-8 strings', 'Generated UTF-8 strings', 'Generated ASCII strings', INVALID and GARBAGE sections), so the published run used an uncommitted variant.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated. CMakeLists.txt builds the benchmark target utf8_bench from test/bench.cpp with -DBUILD_TESTS=ON at CXX_STANDARD 23 and sets no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE or optimization flags; ICU4C is found through pkg-config (icu-uc icu-i18n icu-io), version not stated.
corrections.caveats: First-party single-run README timings with no CPU model, compiler, flags, ICU version or repetition count; no committed benchmark revision prints the README's section headers. The README's '5x-10x' headline contradicts its own table (4.1x to 23x). Benchmark design favours ucstrcase: half of the timed calls compare a pointer with itself and hit an 's == t' early return in ucstrncasecmp, ICU is charged for constructing UTF-16 icu::UnicodeString objects from char* inside the timed loop, and random-string tests end at the first differing byte for ucstrcase but not for ICU. Work is not equivalent: ucstrcase uses Unicode 15.0.0 simple case folding (src/ucstrcase.c caseFold, .tables.json) while UnicodeString::caseCompare with U_FOLD_CASE_DEFAULT uses full case folding, so pairs such as German sharp s vs 'ss' compare equal in ICU but not in ucstrcase. strcasecmp is libc and locale-dependent; which libc was used is unstated. 8 commits, all on 2024-07-04, 0 stars; adapted from Charlie Vieth's Go library strcase (not a GitHub fork). Category: Unicode text processing (case-insensitive UTF-8 comparison), wave 3's unicode-utf8 category with an ICU baseline, not font shaping or layout.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly, but the benchmark has design flaws that inflate the ratios (self-comparison pointer short-circuit for half the calls, ICU conversion cost inside the loop, simple vs full folding); not invalid enough to reject since the comparisons do real work on the other half of calls, so kept at C with a strong shortcoming. Category for the orchestrator: Unicode text processing (wave 3 unicode-utf8, ICU baseline), not shaping. License MIT verified from LICENSE (a stale Unlicense comment in CMakeLists.txt is template residue); last commit 2024-07-04, stale.

tier_reason: First-party README chart (doc/neon_utf8_nfd.png) of xxutf_utf8_nfd vs icu_utf8_nfd produced by public benchmark code (bin/benchmark/benchmark.zig, ICU calls in bin/common/shim.c, inputs in bin/common/inputs) with the Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseFast build stated in build.zig, but no CPU model, ICU version or ICU build flags, so not A. Values exist only as bar heights; no numeric table or result file is committed.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README claims 'the fastest open source implementations of the supported algorithms' and shows one bar chart, doc/neon_utf8_nfd.png (NFD on UTF-8, ARM NEON, GB/s). Values measured from bar pixel heights (derived from page data; 1 pixel = 0.049 GB/s on the 0-35 axis, so each value is +/-0.05 GB/s and the small ICU bars carry 10-20% uncertainty): Arabic 1.91 vs 0.54 GB/s (about 3.5x), Japanese 2.69 vs 0.78 (3.4x), Chinese 4.06 vs 1.03 (4.0x), Hindi 2.59 vs 0.68 (3.8x), Russian 2.44 vs 0.54 (4.5x), Hebrew 2.35 vs 0.64 (3.7x), Korean 0.78 vs 0.24 (3.2x), Latin 34.85 vs 0.34 (about 100x) for xxUTF vs ICU4C. Latin.txt is pure-ASCII lorem ipsum (already NFD), so the Latin bar measures an ASCII pass-through against ICU's UTF-8 to UTF-16 to UTF-8 round trip.
corrections.workload: NFD normalization of UTF-8 text from eight real-text files in bin/common/inputs (Arabic, Chinese, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Russian; e.g. Latin.txt 86,940 bytes pure ASCII, Arabic.txt 81,685 bytes, Korean.txt 66,600 bytes). bin/benchmark/benchmark.zig feeds each file in 4096-byte chunks (trimmed to code-point boundaries), times each chunk with the awake clock and sums per pass, 1000 timed passes after 50 warm-up passes, and reports mean throughput in GiB/s labelled GB/s. The ICU side (IcuNormalizerUtf8) runs u_strFromUTF8, unorm2_normalize with the NFD instance and u_strToUTF8 per chunk into stack buffers; xxUTF works on UTF-8 directly. The README's link to /benchmarks/inputs is stale.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig 0.16.0 build system: 'zig build bench' compiles the xxUTF C amalgamation with ReleaseFast (forced to ReleaseFast if the build mode is Debug), -Wall -Wextra ... -Werror and -DXXUTF_IMPLEMENTATION_NEON=1 on NEON targets (build.zig); ICU4C is linked dynamically as the system icu-uc library, version and build flags not stated.
corrections.caveats: No numeric table or result file: values come from a PNG chart and are approximate (+/-0.05 GB/s per bar). CPU model, OS, ICU version and ICU build flags are not stated; the README only says 'a machine supporting ARM NEON' and asks users to match ICU's Unicode version to xxUTF's (Unicode 17.0.0). The chart was last regenerated in commit 4d1689f 'Improve ASCII normalization' (2026-06-26), and the next commit 5d54cc2 'Fix edge case bugs induced by previous commit' fixed the NEON UTF-8 ASCII fast path (missing '*out_length += 63' and 'last_ccc = 0' resets), so the chart was measured on code later fixed for correctness bugs (the fix adds a few scalar operations per block and probably changes speed little). The Latin bar (about 100x) is pure-ASCII already-normalized text and reflects a pass-through, not decomposition work; per-chunk timing of 4 KiB at about 35 GB/s is roughly 110 ns per timed interval (derived), so timer resolution affects that bar. ICU is charged for UTF-8 to UTF-16 and back conversion around unorm2_normalize; ICU's C++ Normalizer2::normalizeUTF8 was not tried. Unpublished ICU case-fold and UTF-16 benchmark variants are biased against ICU (ucasemap_open/close or ucnv_open/close inside every timed chunk, and ucnv transcoding of UTF-16 input). The work is equivalent in output: NFD is standard-defined, xxUTF case folding uses full folding (CaseFolding.txt C and F entries, Turkic and simple skipped) like ICU's U_FOLD_CASE_DEFAULT, and the AFL++ fuzzer (test/fuzz.c) checks every output against ICU4C. Alpha status per README with a security review pending; 15 stars. Category: Unicode text processing (normalization and case folding), wave 3's unicode-utf8 category with an ICU baseline, not font shaping or layout.

notes: Record accurate: the eyeballed values match the chart within one pixel; pinned down with pixel measurements (no numeric table or result file exists).
